title: CAT 2022 Question Paper (Slot 1, PYQ) - Quantitative Ability - Number System
subject: Quantitative Ability

questions.q: For natural numbers $x,y$, and $z$, if $xy + yz = 19$ and $yz + xz = 51$, then the minimum possible value of $xyz$ is
questions.explain: From $y(x+z)=19$, since 19 is prime and they are natural numbers, either $y=1, x+z=19$ or $y=19, x+z=1$. Since $x,z$ are natural numbers, $x+z \ge 2$, so $y$ must be 1 and $x+z=19$. Substitute into the second equation: $z(y+x) = 51$. With $y=1$, $z(1+x)=51$. We know $x = 19-z$, so $z(20-z)=51 \Rightarrow z^2 - 20z + 51 = 0 \Rightarrow (z-3)(z-17) = 0$. So $z=3$ (giving $x=16$) or $z=17$ (giving $x=2$). We want minimum $xyz$. If $z=3, x=16$, $xyz = 16 \times 1 \times 3 = 48$. If $z=17, x=2$, $xyz = 2 \times 1 \times 17 = 34$. The minimum value is 34.

questions.q: Let $A$ be the largest positive integer that divides all the numbers of the form $3^k + 4^k + 5^k$ and $B$ be the largest positive integer that divides all the numbers of the form $4^k + 3(4^k) + 4^{k+2}$, where $k$ is any positive integer. Then $(A + B)$ equals
questions.explain: For $A$: evaluate $3^k + 4^k + 5^k$ at $k=1$, giving $3+4+5=12$. For $k=2$, $9+16+25=50$. The GCD of 12 and 50 is 2. So $A = 2$. For $B$: $4^k + 3(4^k) + 4^{k+2} = 4^k(1 + 3 + 16) = 4^k(20)$. For $k=1$, it is $4(20)=80$. Since it divides *all* such numbers for any $k$, the minimum factor shared is for $k=1$, so $B = 80$. Then $A + B = 2 + 80 = 82$.
